analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject, and יְהִי מְאֹרֹת (“Let there be lights”) begins the direct speech introduced by וַיֹּאמֶר.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים, the third-person masculine singular verb וַיֹּאמֶר identifies God as the single speaker who commands the lights to appear.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with singular agreement.

analysis.evidence: After וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלֹהִים (“God said”), יְהִי introduces the command for מְאֹרֹת (“lights”) to come into existence in the expanse of the heavens. The singular verb precedes its plural subject.
analysis.morphology: Qal jussive, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: God calls for מְאֹרֹת in the expanse of the heavens to distinguish day from night. The plural וְהָיוּ refers back to these celestial lights, which are to mark appointed times, days, and years.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, masculine plural absolute, with the plural ending ־ֹת.

analysis.evidence: בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם means “in the expanse of the heavens.” The construct noun is linked to הַשָּׁמַיִם, and the phrase locates the lights (מְאֹרֹת).
analysis.morphology: Prefixed preposition בִּ “in” + masculine singular construct noun.

analysis.evidence: בִּרְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמַיִם places the lights “in the expanse of the sky,” where they distinguish day from night.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine plural noun in the absolute state.

draft.change: Add the Hebrew verb בָּדַל with its Hiphil sense of separating.
draft.definition: To separate one thing from another.
draft.evidence: In Gen.1.4, God separates light from darkness. The repeated בֵּין introduces each member of the pair.

analysis.evidence: לְהַבְדִּיל gives the purpose of the lights. בֵּין הַיּוֹם וּבֵין הַלָּיְלָה identifies what they are to separate, the day and the night.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil infinitive construct with prefixed לְ expressing purpose
analysis.sense: to separate one thing from another

analysis.evidence: In לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַיּוֹם וּבֵין הַלָּיְלָה, “to distinguish between day and night,” the marked בֵּין introduces day as the first of the two things the lights distinguish.
analysis.morphology: Preposition in the form בֵּין, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַיּוֹם וּבֵין הַלָּיְלָה, the lights are to distinguish the day from the night. The pairing identifies הַיּוֹם as the daylight portion of the cycle.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: daylight, the day as against night

analysis.evidence: In לְהַבְדִּיל בֵּין הַיּוֹם וּבֵין הַלָּיְלָה, וּבֵין introduces night as the second member of the pair the lights are to distinguish, day and night.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ prefixed to the preposition בֵין.

analysis.evidence: The plural verb refers back to מְאֹרֹת, the lights. The לְ in לְאֹתֹת specifies their function: they are to serve as signs. The rest of the clause extends that function to marking appointed times, days, and years.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person common plural, with prefixed וְ (weqatal), continuing the directive introduced by יְהִי.

analysis.evidence: In וְהָיוּ לְאֹתֹת, the lights are the subject of וְהָיוּ, and לְ introduces their function: they are to serve as signs. The following references to appointed times, days, and years place that function in the context of marking time.
analysis.morphology: Preposition לְ prefixed to a common noun of both genders, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: The lights distinguish day from night and mark appointed times alongside days and years. This sequence supports a calendrical sense. The verse names no particular feast.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ ‘and’ + preposition לְ־ ‘for’ + masculine plural absolute noun מוֹעֲדִים.

analysis.evidence: וּלְיָמִים is paired with וְשָׁנִים (“and years”), identifying days as units of time marked by the lights in the sky. Earlier in the verse, הַיּוֹם is paired with הַלָּיְלָה and means daylight.
analysis.morphology: וּ־ (conjunction “and”) + לְ־ (preposition “for”) + יָמִים (masculine plural absolute noun)

analysis.evidence: The lights in the sky mark units of time. In וּלְיָמִים וְשָׁנִים, “for days and years,” שָׁנִים names the longer cycle paired with days.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a feminine plural absolute noun.
analysis.sense: year, the round of the seasons
